result.title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
result.comment: Accepted at the Sim2Science workshop, NeurIPS 2026. Code: https://github.com/haarisamian/walrus-forgetting-paper
result.summary: Scientific foundation models (SciFMs) have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of PDEs, including the ability to efficiently adapt to unseen data distributions with additional finetuning. As with all neural architectures, finetuning such models comes with the risk of catastrophic forgetting, whereby adapting to new tasks degrades prior knowledge of the model. We study catastrophic forgetting in Walrus-1.3B, a SciFM for continuum dynamics, over the course of a two-stage sim-to-real adaptation: first finetuning on simulated flow around a cylinder and then adapting to experimental data of the same system. We find that finetuning on the simulations rapidly degrades rollout performance on the original pretraining datasets, with one-step errors increasing up to 35x after just 20 epochs. Subsequent adaptation to real data further erodes performance on the simulated task. We characterize the potential drivers of forgetting, such as dataset dependence and task representation similarity. We then show that replaying as little as 1% simulated data during real-data finetuning recovers most of the lost simulation performance while retaining effective adaptation to the experimental dynamics. Our results identify catastrophic forgetting as a practical obstacle to sim-to-real adaptation of SciFMs and show that lightweight replay strategies significantly improve retention.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 PDE 科学基础模型 Walrus-1.3B 在两阶段 sim-to-real 微调中的灾难性遗忘：仅在模拟圆柱绕流上微调 20 轮即使原始预训练任务的一步误差最高放大 35 倍，随后迁移真实数据又进一步损害模拟任务；作者分析数据依赖与任务表示相似性等成因，并证明混入 1% 模拟数据回放即可恢复大部分模拟性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文的回放/排练策略与「任务表示相似性驱动遗忘」分析，可能为 VLM 在多阶段微调（如视觉证据筛选或推理轨迹训练）中保留既有推理与视觉能力提供可核查的线索，但领域与模态差异较大，需先确认机制是否可迁移。
